newsitem.title: USA: Latest "Trek" movie boldly opens at top of box office.
newsitem.headline: Latest "Trek" movie boldly opens at top of box office.

text.p: "Star Trek: First Contact" opened at the top of the weekend box office with a take of $30.45 million, according to studio estimates released on Sunday.
The three-day figures for the critically acclaimed movie were the highest for any of the eight big screen entries in the sci-fi franchise, said Paramount Pictures, a unit of Viacom Inc..
The previous record was held by "Generations," which earned $23.12 million in its first three days in 1994, excluding Thursday night previews, and went on to make $75.7 million.

Last week's number one, "Space Jam," slipped to second with $16.6 million. The comedic mixture of live action and animation has a 10-day gross of $48.6 million. The movie is released by Warner Bros., a unit of Time Warner Inc..
Also down a notch was the Mel Gibson thriller "Ransom," with $13.7 million. In its third weekend, the Walt Disney Co. kidnapping saga has earned $86.2 million.
Opening in fourth was the Arnold Schwarzenegger Christmas comedy "Jingle All The Way," with $12.2 million.
Despite being slayed by film critics, the movie is Schwarzenegger's best comedy opening. His previous best was "Kindergarten Cop," which opened in 1990 with $11.2 million.
"Jingle All The Way" is released by 20th Century Fox, a unit of News Corp..

Down two places to fifth was Barbra Streisand's "The Mirror Has Two Faces," which earned $8.2 million in its second weekend. Its 10-day total is $24.3 million. The movie is released by Sony Corp.'s TriStar Pictures.
Opening in limited release, on seven screens, was the Australian drama "Shine," based on the true story of pianist prodigy David Helfgott.
The movie, which is released by Time Warner's Fine Line Features, earned $164,000 for a per-screen average of $23,429.
